implementation_notes: Scala 3's opaque type aliases are the pattern in the language: outside the defining scope the alias is seen only as its bound, so a String is not accepted where UserId is expected, while inside the scope the value is used directly with no wrapper and no allocation. The docs present them as the replacement for Scala 2 value classes. Put the smart constructor in the companion object - the only place that may see the representation - and add behaviour with extension methods.
code_sketch:
object ids:
  opaque type UserId = Long

  object UserId:
    def parse(raw: Long): UserId =
      require(raw > 0, "user id must be positive")
      raw

  extension (id: UserId) def value: Long = id
pitfalls: The abstraction is scope-based: anywhere inside the defining object or file the alias is transparent, so keep the definition and its helpers in one small unit.
Opaque types erase to the underlying type, so equals/hashCode/toString come from the value and reflection or asInstanceOf can cross the boundary; primitives may still box when they erase to Any.
Operations must be defined at the definition site (like value classes), so an outside party cannot add a method to the opaque type without an extension in scope.

variants.name: value class extending AnyVal
variants.idiom_name: final class UserId(val value: Long) extends AnyVal
variants.implementation_notes: On Scala 2 the equivalent is a value class: a class extending AnyVal with exactly one val parameter and no other state, which the compiler erases to the underlying value while preserving the distinct type. It is the documented Scala 2 answer and the migration path to opaque types; the costs are its constraints (one public val, no other fields, universal traits only) and boxing wherever the value is used generically.
pitfalls: Value classes box whenever they are stored in an array, used as a generic argument or assigned to Any, so they are not allocation-free in those positions.
equals/hashCode follow the underlying value and the class cannot be extended meaningfully; pattern matching and reflection see the erased form.
